images.title: The quadrilateral family rings
images.purpose: Shows the nested family rings: rectangles and rhombuses overlap in squares inside parallelograms, and kites meet parallelograms exactly in the rhombuses.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large rounded ring with overlapping rings inside, each labelled once at its edge.
images.exact_structure: One large rounded rectangle in thin grey (#6B7280) outline labelled Quadrilaterals at its top left. Inside it, a large oval in teal (#0072B2) outline labelled Parallelograms, filling the left two thirds. A second oval in dark outline, labelled Kites, sits on the right, entirely inside Quadrilaterals, and crosses the right edge of the Parallelograms oval. The lens where Kites and Parallelograms overlap is lightly filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) and labelled Rhombuses; there is no separate Rhombuses oval. A smaller oval in amber (#E69F00) outline, labelled Rectangles, sits inside Parallelograms on the left and reaches partway into the Rhombuses lens. The part of Rectangles inside the lens is filled a deeper reddish purple and labelled Squares. Each region is labelled once. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: A figure belongs to every ring it fits: squares are rectangles and rhombuses, and rhombuses are both parallelograms and kites.
images.description: Shows the nested family rings: rectangles and rhombuses overlap in squares inside parallelograms, and kites meet parallelograms exactly in the rhombuses.
images.context: Kite ∩ parallelogram = rhombus; kite ∩ rectangle = square; not every kite is a rhombus.

image_decisions.why: The sorter's nested rings, with kites added as this practice asks, in one clean diagram.
